title: Plea bargaining in India - why lawyers rarely use this option
p1:
Many people think every criminal case must end with a long trial.

But India has a legal option where an accused can negotiate a quicker resolution. So why is plea bargaining still rarely used?
p2: The surprising part is that plea bargaining has existed in India for years, yet many lawyers and accused persons do not choose it. The reason is not just lack of awareness. Concerns about admitting guilt, social stigma, and doubts about whether the outcome will truly be better often make people hesitant.
p3:
Plea bargaining allows an accused in certain eligible cases to accept responsibility in exchange for a possible lesser punishment or faster disposal of the case. It is not a shortcut available for every offence. The practical challenge is that many people still see a negotiated settlement as a sign of weakness rather than a strategic legal decision.

A good lawyer evaluates whether fighting the case or choosing plea bargaining better serves the client's interests.
conclusion: Do you think plea bargaining should be used more often in India, or does admitting guilt create too many risks?
